name: Guardian genius crossword No 162
preamble: The puzzle is a tribute to two people whose names appear in the completed grid. (There is a numerical connection between them.) X and two of his products are in a combination of solutions. Y appears step-wise; his nom de plume is formed by the first letters of solutions to the asterisked clues in reverse order. His best known product appears twice in the grid, once homophonically.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: *I will get so many together for sex

blocks.clueFragment: I will get so many together for sex
blocks.note: surface reading: a number of people pairing off for sex
setter's reading: the Roman numeral I joined with this number makes VI, six, and sex is Latin for six

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of how many partners they will round up for an orgy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex is the Latin word for six; I beside the Roman numeral V reads VI, so the number that joins I to make six is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: So many is a stand-in for a quantity, here the count that turns Roman one into Roman six.

clue.text: See 12 across
Cabled vehicle on route up carrying Australian music maker

indicators.note: in a down light, going up the route means reading the word from bottom to top
a vehicle carrying a passenger holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a tram runs on cables or overhead wires
Oz is informal for Australia or Australian

explanation.surface: A cable car climbing a route carries an Australian musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart, the Austrian composer, is a maker of music in the broadest sense.

clue.text: Remarkable force altered yellow tincture's density

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
or is the heraldic tincture gold, shown as yellow
d is the physics symbol for density

explanation.surface: A striking change in a yellow dye's density, as a chemist might note it.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold, which heraldry paints yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of record is worth noting, so notable or remarkable, as in a feat of record.

clue.text: *Press carpet, after spinning more repulsive

indicators.note: spinning turns the string round like a wheel, so letters from the end come round to the front

blocks.note: to lie is to press flat against a surface
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: Pressing a carpet after a spin in the washer makes it look worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are joined, then the last three letters are rotated round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier is the comparative of ugly, meaning more unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Hip flask initially spotted and ignored by golf club further on

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
the word and is noticed in the club's name and then dropped from it

blocks.note: in means fashionable, or hip
the first letter of flask
the R&A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, with its ampersand left out

explanation.surface: A hip flask is noticed and overlooked by the members of a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club at St Andrews in Scotland; the 'and' in its name is the part spotted and ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra is Latin used in texts to mean below or later, referring a reader to a passage further on.

clue.text: 1 by 1 whenever T's put after female name

indicators.note: put after says the following pieces are placed behind the one that comes next in the clue

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for female
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'
the letter T spelt out
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A rule about adding a T after a girl's name, one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 refers to 1 Down, FIVE: the digit 1 placed by 5 writes 15. The 's of T's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing the numeral one beside the numeral five gives the number fifteen, a cross-reference trick.

clue.text: Announcement of Pac-Man?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out loud, so the game's name is taken by its sound

blocks.note: said out loud this is pack

explanation.surface: A question about what the arcade hero Pac-Man has to declare.
explanation.walkthrough: Pac-Man spoken is 'pack man': the man named for a pack, of wolves. Wolfgang is Mozart's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang is a German male forename, built from words for wolf and band, so it names a man.

clue.text: *Film in the 14 divides Americans

indicators.note: dividing something splits it apart, leaving the other piece sitting between its halves

blocks.note: A and US, both abbreviations for American
14 Down's light reads CAN, and a film in the can is finished, made

explanation.surface: A finished film splits opinion among Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: In the can is film jargon for a movie that has been shot and finished; the cross-reference supplies the can.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the 1984 Milos Forman film about Mozart's rivalry with Salieri.

clue.text: Piece of work, in brief, for teacher

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their breaks

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of brief, through for, into the start of teacher

explanation.surface: A short piece of work handed in to a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort can mean a piece of work produced, as in 'a decent effort'.

clue.text: Terms omitted from warning about St David's Day prayer

indicators.note: terms are ends or limits, so the outer letters are dropped from the word
about means around, so the trimmed word wraps the date

blocks.note: a caveat is a warning
1 March, written Mar 1 with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A warning about Welsh national day is cut short, then offered up as a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: St David's Day, the Welsh national day, is 1 March. Ave Maria is also a Schubert song and one of Mozart's motets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is the Catholic prayer to the Virgin.

clue.text: Heritage affair comically enacted with groom?

definitions.text: Heritage affair comically enacted with groom?

indicators.note: a comic staging plays freely with its material, so the words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historic romance staged for laughs with a bridegroom at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the opera: a comic wedding plot, with Figaro as the groom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's comic opera stages the wedding day of the servant Figaro, a groom's affair played for laughs.

clue.text: Jack Jones of Bow or the Fox of Falkirk?

blocks.note: first meaning: in Cockney slang, on your Jack Jones and on your ... both mean on your own
second meaning: a Scots word for a fox

explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, so the phrase means Cockney rhyming slang, where Jack Jones and Tod (Sloan, a jockey) both stand for 'own'. Falkirk is a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is the Cockney equivalent of Jack Jones in 'on your own' and the Scots dialect name for a fox.

clue.text: Alien in outer space wanting tip from Peter Sellers

indicators.note: something alien is strange and foreign, so these letters are made unfamiliar by rearrangement
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
a tip is the very end of something, here the opening letter of the name

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Peter

explanation.surface: An alien in outer space wants advice from the comic actor Peter Sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers looks like a single name, but Peter supplies a letter and Sellers alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctioneers conduct sales, selling goods to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Do without whichever gully (but preserve that one?)

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to do someone is to con or cheat them
any, as in 'take any you like'

explanation.surface: Manage without whatever ravine, but keep that one.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket gives a second route: preserve is CAN, as in tinning food, and that one is YON, which is how the answer splits across the two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley, a big gully cut by a river.

clue.text: *Waste a long time in prison

blocks.note: dung is animal waste
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Wasting years locked up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell for holding prisoners, so a kind of prison.

clue.text: *Hateful Englishman's last to join fellow noonday exposer up

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word it follows
in a down light, up means the phrase is written from bottom to top
to join says one piece is attached to another

blocks.note: from Noel Coward's song: mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun
the final letter of Englishman

explanation.surface: A spiteful Englishman teams up with another who stays out in the midday heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Coward's song says mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun, so the Englishman's companion out at noon is a mad dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Goddamn is a strong intensifier for something cursed or detested, so it serves as hateful.

clue.text: See 12 across
Headless corpse's sent west for certain journey

indicators.note: headless means the word loses its first letter
in an across light, going west is moving right to left, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a corpse is a body, with the 's kept
yes is an answer of certainty

explanation.surface: A beheaded body is sent off west on a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent west' here applies to certain alone, while corpse's just loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is a long wandering voyage, named after Odysseus's journey home.

clue.text: A sample of two hundred working parties in Auckland?

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken out, so the letters are drawn from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of two and the start of hundred

explanation.surface: A survey sampling two hundred people at work parties in an Auckland setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Auckland is in New Zealand, a hint at a Maori word.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand an ohu is a communal work group, from the Maori word for a cooperative team.

clue.text: Feature of brutish creature who is outspoken cutting prime minister up

indicators.note: outspoken words are spoken out, so the phrase is taken by its sound
in a down light, up means writing the name from bottom to top
cutting into something puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Theresa May, UK Prime Minister when the puzzle appeared
said in a Scots accent, who sounds like hoo

explanation.surface: A trait of a boorish brute who speaks his mind and undercuts the PM.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoos are the brutish humans in Swift's Gulliver's Travels; Theresa May was the UK prime minister in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahooism is the coarse, uncivilised behaviour typical of a yahoo, the brute of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Germany initially quits by itself

indicators.note: initially says the next piece comes first, ahead of the one before it

blocks.note: to be quits with someone is to be square, even
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany quits first, going it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: With FIFTEEN at 7 Down this gives fifteensquared, the blog run by Gaufrid; fifteen squared is 225, the Mozart anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A number squared is multiplied by itself, so by itself is a mathematical paraphrase.

clue.text: See 14
With mud for slinging, how to spread rumour?

definitions.text: With mud for slinging, how to spread rumour?

indicators.note: slinging throws things about, so these letters are flung into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on smearing someone: with plenty of mud to sling, how do you get gossip going?
explanation.walkthrough: Mud-slinging is spreading damaging rumours, so the whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumours spread by people telling each other, informally from person to person, which is passing it by word of mouth.

clue.text: They're last ones for supper a half-hour before marching ones are issued!

definitions.text: They're last ones for supper a half-hour before

blocks.clueFragment: They're last ones for supper a half-hour before
blocks.note: first meaning: last ..., the pub's final call for drinks before closing
second meaning: marching ..., given to someone dismissed

explanation.walkthrough: Supper means one who sups, a drinker, not an evening meal; last orders are called in a British pub shortly before closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Commands or requests: the barman takes final requests for drinks, and a dismissed person is given instructions to leave.

clue.text: Gaelic poetical figure — or musical one, essentially?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so its central letter is taken

blocks.note: ossia is Italian for 'or', marking an alternative passage in a score
the middle letter of one

explanation.surface: A Gaelic figure in verse, or perhaps a musical one at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossia appears in printed music to offer an easier or alternative version of a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard whose poems James Macpherson claimed to translate in the 1760s.

clue.text: What appears when fiery enclosure's consumed body features?

definitions.text: What appears when fiery enclosure's consumed body features?

indicators.note: consumed means used up or eaten away, so those letters vanish from the word

blocks.note: a furnace is an enclosed fire, with the 's kept
faces are features of the body

explanation.surface: A grim question about what is left once a cremation furnace burns away a body.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are scattered through the word, not in one block. Read whole, the clue describes cremation, after which the ashes appear in an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: After a cremation furnace consumes a body, the ashes are handed over in an urn.

clue.text: *Seaweed used as fish feeder, even space filler?

indicators.note: a fish's feed goes inside it, so this piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: ides are freshwater fish of the carp family
alga is a seaweed

explanation.surface: Seaweed served as fish food fills the tank evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide is a European fish, a regular in crosswords. 'Even' fits because such a gas spreads uniformly through its container.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect theoretical gas expands to fill any container uniformly, making it an even filler of space.

clue.text: Detective's drunk inn out of Pinot Noir, unfortunately

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so those letters are taken from the wine's name
an unfortunate outcome has gone awry, so what remains is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of inn, drunk because they are scattered through the wine rather than together

explanation.surface: A detective is drunk, kicked out of an inn after too much Pinot Noir.
explanation.walkthrough: Drunk tells the solver the removed letters are not together; they come out singly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian private detective.

clue.text: Bishop's Bar in Bath bars bishops!

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
to bar is to exclude, so these letters are kept out

blocks.note: a bath is a tub
but means except, as bar does
B is chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's bar in the city of Bath refuses entry to bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar goes inside after the first letter of bath's synonym, then both Bs drop out. Bath is also an English cathedral city, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu was the South African Anglican archbishop and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: *Resistance encountered by radio broadcast about new surgeon's heart bypass

indicators.note: one thing meeting another sets them side by side
broadcast scatters widely, so these letters are spread into a new order
the heart of a word is its central letter
about means around, so the rearranged word surrounds the other pieces

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written
n is the abbreviation for new
the middle letter of surgeon

explanation.surface: A radio report on a new surgeon's heart bypass meets resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart bypass reads as surgery, but bypass alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road is a road circling a town so traffic can avoid its centre, a type of bypass.

clue.text: Sun a little upset for Nobel Peace Prize winner

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: S is short for Sunday or sun
taken as written
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper is slightly put out about a peace laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: Anwar Sadat shared the 1978 prize with Menachem Begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat, Egypt's president, won the Nobel Peace Prize for the Camp David accords with Israel.
